exposure: mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental delivery)
cohort: The study included 1750 postnatal mothers who had spontaneous vaginal deliveries and were accessing postnatal care.
finding: The prevalence of episiotomy among the study population was 49.7%, which is significantly higher than the 10% recommended by the World Health Organisation, indicating potential overuse.
mod_finding: Spontaneous vaginal delivery (SVD) and instrumental deliveries were both associated with a reduced likelihood of episiotomy in the multivariate analysis.
